name: DNA-BOT: low-cost automated DNA assembly on an Opentrons OT-2 (Imperial/Freemont, 2020)
brief: An automated DNA assembly platform for synthetic biology: one benchtop open-source liquid-handling robot with magnetic-bead and temperature modules, plus an external thermocycler, assembles up to 96 genetic constructs per run, purifies them and transforms bacteria by heat shock, ready for colony picking.

cost.original: around $8k for the OT-2 including all required modules and pipettes (2020)
cost.excludes_note: OT-2 with modules and pipettes only. The thermocycler, incubators, plates and consumables are excluded (consumables quoted separately at $1.50-$5.50 per construct).

notes: price_basis=configured, set from the source wording ("the OT-2 including all required modules and pipettes") before base/configured catalog prices were researched. Single-instrument price check: the reported figure is one OT-2 with pipettes/modules, so this tests the catalog price band, not whole-lab design. includes covers 'instruments' because the catalog files liquid handlers there. Verified 3 Oct 2026 via Europe PMC full text of Storch et al., ACS Synth. Biol./Synth. Biol. 2020: "At the time of writing, the OT-2 including all required modules and pipettes costs around $8k." Also "consumables cost per construct was as low as $1.50 or $5.50". Automated run: 1578 pipetting steps, 38 magnetic bead purifications, 96 heat-shock transformations. Throughput value is runs of up to 96 constructs (per run, not per day). Cost is a robot price, not a lab build.

equipment.rationale: The single OT-2 the paper prices.
